body.objective: Replace the declared two-angle BT detector effect by an explicit finite pointer Hamiltonian whose interaction time selects epsilon and whose interferometric setting selects the relative angle phase.
activates: a bounded self-adjoint apparatus interaction on the BT two-angle carrier and one pointer qubit
exact phase selection through a conjugated symmetric/antisymmetric angle basis
a physical finite-device realization of the q6 and relative-q8 detector effects
body.current_gate: For phase z=e^{i phi}, form P_minus(phi)=|c1-z c2><c1-z c2|/2 and H_int=g P_minus(phi) tensor sigma_y. Exponentiate it exactly for theta=g tau, prepare pointer |0>, and derive both Kraus operators. Prove their effects are E_click=P_plus(phi)+cos(theta)^2 P_minus(phi) and E_no=sin(theta)^2 P_minus(phi), including completeness, phase calibration and the q6/q8 pullback.
body.stop_condition: Land an exact COEFFICIENT_COMPUTED finite-apparatus certificate, method-distinct verifier, mutation tests, report and Papers 05/06 update. State explicitly that this is an external finite detector coupled to the BT output modes, not a term derived from the public closed-system BT Hamiltonian or a spacetime-local detector model.
body.forbid: no abstract Naimark existence theorem called a Hamiltonian derivation; no apparatus knob called a BT prediction; no finite two-mode interaction promoted to public BT evolution, LSZ, Eq. 19, gravity, QME or LORENTZIAN-CAUSAL physics
body.resource_hint: Because P_minus(phi) is a projector, exp[-i theta P_minus(phi) tensor sigma_y]=P_plus(phi) tensor I+P_minus(phi) tensor [cos(theta)I-i sin(theta)sigma_y]. With pointer |0>, K_click=P_plus+cos(theta)P_minus and K_no=sin(theta)P_minus. Thus E_click=I-sin(theta)^2 P_minus and E_no=sin(theta)^2 P_minus. At calibrated phase phi=delta of X2=x(1,e^{i delta}), E_click X2=X2. A mismatch Delta=delta-phi suppresses the leading probability by epsilon sin^2(Delta/2).
